articles.title: 'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski testifies he was beaten, tortured during alleged kidnapping
articles.summary: Self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski described being beaten with a gun and tortured with knives and a lighter in the back of a truck as he began his testimony at the trial of his alleged…

image.caption: Aiden Pleterski, who went by the moniker 'Crypto King,' enters the Superior Court of Justice building, in Toronto, on Oct. 5. (Evan Mitsui/CBC)

blocks.text: Toronto·New

Self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski described being beaten with a gun and tortured with knives and a lighter in the back of a truck as he began his testimony at the trial of his alleged kidnappers Friday in Toronto.
Jury sees video of Pleterski begging for his life at trial of alleged kidnappers
Warning: This story contains distressing details about torture and graphic images
"[I was] very scared, scared I'm going to die, scared for my life, in survival mode essentially," Pleterski told the Ontario Superior Court about how he felt at the time.
The Crown played a 13-second video for the jury, which showed Pleterski on his knees begging for his life while a man pointed a gun at him and counted down from three.
Before reaching one, the man appears to fire the gun beside Pleterski's head.
"It didn't hit me, but I know it was very loud and there was a constant ringing in my left ear," Pleterski testified. "When he shot the firearm I didn't know if I was shot or not."
Akil Heywood, Alfredo Paladino and Rakeem Henry are all charged with kidnapping and extorting Pleterski over the course of three days in early December 2022.
'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski begs for his life during kidnapping

Paladino and Henry are also charged with firearms offences, the aggravated assault of Pleterski, assaulting him with a weapon, and assault causing bodily harm over that same period. All three men have pleaded not guilty.
Pleterski, 27, was convicted of fraud last month in connection with more than $30 million he took from investors to trade on their behalf, but he's yet to be sentenced.

He told the court that Heywood invested between $300,000 and $400,000 and allegedly started threatening him in texts and phone calls about getting that money back in the beginning to the middle of 2022.
Pleterski also testified that Heywood was appointed as one of the five creditor inspectors tasked with overseeing his bankruptcy proceeding.
'Driving force'

In its opening statement, the Crown alleged Heywood was the "driving force" behind the plan to kidnap Pleterski and that evidence would show another man — who is not part of the trial — was the lead kidnapper and that Paladino and Henry carried it out alongside him.

Pleterski identified Heywood, Paladino and Henry in the courtroom Friday as Crown prosecutor Julia De Vuono walked him through the events leading to the alleged kidnapping and what Pleterski said happened to him during it.
From left to right, Alfredo Paladino, Akil Heywood and Rakeem Henry are accused of kidnapping and extorting Pleterski in December 2022. (Evan Mitsui/CBC, Instagram/atlanticmastoronto)

Pleterski described how he met a man he was introduced to as "Slime" a couple of weeks before the alleged kidnapping who said he wanted help converting cryptocurrency into cash. The pair began communicating and organized a meeting at the Ritz Carlton hotel in downtown Toronto in late 2022, according to Pleterski.
He testified that "Slime" attended the meeting with two other men, including one he later pointed out as Henry in the courtroom.

A couple of days later, on Dec. 5, Pleterski said he received a message from "Slime" asking to meet up about the cryptocurrency. Pleterski testified "Slime" picked him up in downtown Toronto in a Dodge Ram but this time, after he got in the backseat, "Slime" got in beside him and pulled out a gun.
He said Henry was on the other side of him in the backseat and also had a pistol on his lap. Pleterski identified Paladino as the driver.
Sandeep Gupta, Pleterski's former landlord, testified on Tuesday and Thursday at the trial of three men accused of kidnapping the self-described 'Crypto King.' (Pam Davies/CBC)

Pleterski said he was zip-tied and reusable garbage bags were put over his head at various points. He testified the truck got on the Gardiner Expressway and that, while in transit, "Slime" made a call.
"I knew instantly it was AK, or Akil Heywood," said Pleterski, about hearing the voice on the phone, which he testified was on speaker.
Pleterski testified that Heywood said "Where the F is my money, pussy?" and told him: "You're either going to pay with your money or you're going to pay with your life."

From there Pleterski explained how he told the kidnappers that his former landlord Sandeep Gupta was "hiding a bunch of assets, [I] just need to call him." Although in court, Pleterski said that was not true.

On Tuesday, the jury heard audio of a 911 call Gupta made during a phone call with Pleterski. Pleterski testified "Slime" was instructing him on what to say during that call, including telling him he needed $2-3 million from Gupta.
The Crown asked Pleterski why he didn't tell Gupta he was kidnapped.
"If I told him on the phone that I was kidnapped, I was scared that they would kill me," he replied.

items: Crypto King's alleged kidnappers’ trial hears call Aiden Pleterski made to landlord asking for $3M

blocks.text: Pleterski wasn't sure whether the phone call with Gupta happened before or after he was taken to a field, where the video of him on his knees was allegedly taken.
In that video, after the gun appears to be fired, Pleterski says "Sandeep has it all."
Gupta testified at the trial Tuesday and Thursday and denied any involvement in Pleterski's Ponzi scheme and denied hiding any money or assets for him.
Pleterski's testimony continued Friday afternoon.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Nicole Brockbank is a reporter for CBC Toronto's Enterprise Unit. She digs up, researches and reports GTA-focused investigative and enterprise stories. nicole.brockbank@cbc.ca

articles.title: Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu of ‘racist’ campaign against Israel’s Arab minority
articles.summary:
Statement a rare instance of a prominent Jewish political leader taking a strong stand in defence of Arab Israelis

Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot accused caretaker premier…

blocks.text: Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot accused caretaker premier Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday of fuelling a “racist” campaign against the country’s Arab minority, after he sought to delegitimise the community’s lawmakers by linking them to Hamas.
Eisenkot’s statement was a rare instance of a prominent Jewish political leader taking a strong stand in defence of Arab Israelis, who make up more than 20% of the population.

Two Arab-majority parties, Raam and the Joint List, secured a combined 19 seats in last month’s election, winning nearly a sixth of the 120-seat parliament and potentially emerging as kingmakers in efforts by Eisenkot to form a government.
“Arab citizens of Israel are an integral part of the Israeli story,” Eisenkot wrote on X on Friday.
“They have been subjected to a racist and aggressive campaign of delegitimisation, fuelled by the outgoing prime minister and those around him for political purposes,” he added.
“The attempt to marginalise them and vilify them collectively is a profound violation of the principles of civic responsibility.”
Netanyahu and his allies have repeatedly criticised leaders of Arab parties for refusing to describe Hamas as a “terror group” following its unprecedented 7 October 2023 attack on Israel.
All leaders of Arab parties have condemned the attack, in which Arab Israelis – descendants of Palestinians who remained in what became Israel in 1948 – were also among those killed.
Netanyahu has also repeatedly alleged electoral fraud by Arab-majority parties, but electoral authorities have rejected the claims.
In a speech, Netanyahu lamented that the two Arab lists refused to recognise Israel as a Jewish state, although Raam leader Mansour Abbas has done so in the past.
He further claimed that they sought to establish either an “Islamic state” or a “nationalist Palestinian state”.
During the same ceremony, national security minister Itamar Ben Gvir heckled Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen during his oath of allegiance, accusing him of having “pledged allegiance to Hamas”.

“It is entirely legitimate to disagree with representatives of the Arab parties, even to strongly disapprove of some of them. But it is neither legitimate nor acceptable to malign an entire community, and I will not allow it,” Eisenkot said.

President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming a new government on Sunday after consultations in which a majority of political parties, including the two Arab lists, recommended him for the role.
But one of Eisenkot’s rightwing allies, Avigdor Lieberman, has said he will back out of the coalition if Arab Israelis are part of it.
If Eisenkot fails to form a government within 28 days, he may request a 14-day extension. Should he still fall short, the mandate would pass to another lawmaker, most likely Netanyahu.

articles.title: Hungary seizes $19.5m in cash found buried in forests amid graft inquiry
articles.summary:
Anti-corruption agency carried out searches as part of investigation into Orbán-era minister accused of taking bribes

Hungary’s anti-corruption agency said on Friday it had seized cash worth…

blocks.text: Hungary’s anti-corruption agency said on Friday it had seized cash worth $19.5m (£14.8m) buried in forests and hidden elsewhere while investigating an ex-minister of nationalist former leader Viktor Orbán.

Miklós Seszták, Hungary’s minister of national development between 2014 and 2018, is accused of taking bribes in a scheme involving the state transport company, purchasing secondhand buses at inflated prices.

The prime minister, Péter Magyar, won a landslide election victory in April, ending Orbán’s 16 years in power after promising to investigate alleged corruption and abuse of office during his rival’s rule.
Seszták, two other Orbán-era ministers and the former premier’s brother have been taken into custody in different cases as graft inquiries have gathered pace in recent weeks.

The National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH), an anti-graft body with sweeping powers established as part of Magyar’s accountability drive, said it searched multiple locations on Thursday and Friday as part of the criminal proceedings against Seszták.

“During the search, investigators found large amounts of cash: buried in forests, hidden in agricultural and warehouse buildings as well as residential properties, and stored in high-value safes in secluded locations,” the statement said.
“The total amount of cash found during the two-day search was 5,071,632,000 forints, €2,658,350 and US $1,257,100,” it added, bringing the combined value to $19.5m.
NVVH said its staff deposited the cash into the Hungarian State Treasury’s account.
“Upon receipt, 12 Treasury employees spent 8 hours counting the money using 5 counting machines,” finance minister András Kármán said on Facebook.
Magyar hailed the seizure as a potential turning point.
“This officially marks the end of the Fidesz-KDNP mafia!” he said in reference to Orbán’s former governing coalition.
The former leader did not react to the latest development. Orbán had previously denounced the probes targeting his inner circle as “political persecution” aimed at imprisoning him.

blocks.text: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) on Friday issued a ground stop on all national flights. The FAA is the US government agency responsible for air traffic control.
"All departing traffic should remain groundstopped until further notice," the FAA said.
The agency said the ground stop is "due to extraordinary circumstance and reasons for safety."
In a post on X, US Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said the stop was due to a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers.
"FAA technicians are investigating the issue. We will provide immediate updates as we have them."
It's the first nationwide ground stop since January 2023, when the FAA dealt with a system outage. Prior to that, the last ground stop was after the September 11, 2001 terror attacks.

Transportation secretary Sean Duffy said stoppage is due to ‘communication issue’ and that FAA is looking into issue

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has issued a nationwide ground…

blocks.text: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has issued a nationwide ground stop for all flights that are due to take off in the US on Friday, delaying or canceling nearly 7,000 US flights, according to aviation tracker FlightAware.

In a post on X, the US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, said the stoppage is due to “a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers” and that the FAA’s technicians are looking into the matter.

This is the third time all departing flights have been grounded in the US. The first time was on 11 September 2001; the other was in January 2023, when the FAA paused all ⁠domestic departures for less than two hours after a pilot notification system malfunctioned.
The FAA has more than 14,000 air traffic controllers who handle the more than 44,000 flights that take off from airports across the US each day, according to FAA data.

articles.title: As Van Hollen wages a challenge, Senate Democrats are torn on whom to elect as their leader
articles.summary: Maryland senator’s bid against Chuck Schumer for leadership could decide direction of the Democratic party

blocks.text: Ever since Donald Trump returned to the White House, Democratic officeholders and voters alike have been divided over whether their leader in the Senate, Chuck Schumer, is up to the task of taking the president on.

That debate intensified on Thursday, when the Maryland senator Chris Van Hollen announced he will challenge Schumer for the post of Democratic Senate leader, which will become one of the most powerful jobs in Washington when the party takes control of Congress’s upper chamber next year.

The contest between Schumer and Van Hollen is the party’s first major test of unity after its triumph in last week’s midterm elections, in which voters gave Democrats their biggest majorities in both the Senate and House of Representatives in years. Now the party will be forced to confront the two veteran lawmakers’ differing visions on how to use their newly expanded power to confront Trump, advance the party’s agenda and address divisive issues such as the question of aid to Israel.

“Trump’s policies have been fired, but we are still in the position where we need to take advantage of this opportunity. So that does mean closing the trust deficit? … And I don’t think you can close the trust deficit by simply returning to the status quo,” Van Hollen said at a press conference on Friday.

Progressive groups have cheered the 67-year-old Van Hollen’s candidacy, and he’s picked up a handful of endorsements in the hours since he made his bid official. But his prospects are unclear: the senator said he is an “underdog” in the contest, which is set to be decided at a behind-closed-doors caucus meeting scheduled for 1 December.
Schumer, meanwhile, has expressed confidence he’ll win the Democratic caucus’s nod again, and has the support of senators from across the party’s ideological spectrum.

“I welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead,” Schumer, 75, wrote on X after Van Hollen announced his bid. “I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader.”

A New York City native, Schumer won election to the House in 1980, then the Senate in 1998. He became the top Senate Democrat in 2017, when the party was in the minority at the beginning of Trump’s first term. Four years later, Schumer became majority leader under Joe Biden, and managed to win passage of parts of his legislative agenda even though the Democratic caucus was so small it could not lose a single vote on party-line bills.

Trump returned to power in 2025, and it was not long after that Schumer’s leadership came into question. In March of that year, Congress faced a deadline to approve new government funding or cause a shutdown. Though many Democrats believed they had leverage over Trump to win concessions, perhaps over the gutting of the federal government by the “department of government efficiency”, Schumer opted to advance a GOP-backed spending measure, arguing that it was a bad time to shut down the government.

The compromise triggered an explosion of anger at Schumer both from Democrats in the House of Representatives who had rejected the funding compromise, and activist groups who saw it as a sign that Schumer was no longer fit to be leader.

“Senator Schumer has contributed to and led many important accomplishments that Indivisible is grateful for. But with our democracy on the line, he let us, the country and the Democratic party down,” said Ezra Levin, co-executive director of the network of progressive groups.
“Senator Schumer should step aside as leader. Every Democrat in the Senate should call for him to do so, and begin making plans for new leadership immediately.”

The relationship between Schumer and the party base – including some Democratic lawmakers – has yet to recover. Another wave of calls for Schumer to step down arrived later that year, when dissident Senate Democrats decided to end a record-long government shutdown without Republicans meeting any of their demands on healthcare.

Schumer did not publicly endorse their deal, but it was widely believed to have his backing. By the time campaigning for the 2026 midterms began, several candidates were making their opposition to him prominent in their platforms.

In some ways, the tension is a unique consequence of the differences in power between the minority party in the House and Senate. In the former, the party out of power has little recourse to block legislation, but in the latter, the filibuster’s 60-vote threshold makes Schumer a major figure in deciding whether his party plays along with the 53 Republicans in the majority, or obstructs them.

At the same time that Schumer’s standing among Democrats was growing rocky, Van Hollen’s star was ascending. Elected to the Senate from the House in 2016, Van Hollen made national news when he traveled to El Salvador to meet Kilmar Ábrego García, a Salvadorian who had been wrongfully deported from Maryland in the early days of Trump’s mass deportation campaign.
after newsletter promotion

He has joined in criticizing Israel, amid a wider backlash among Democratic voters towards the US ally fueled by accusations it committed a genocide in Gaza. Van Hollen voted against providing bulldozers and bombs to the country, and after a visit to the Gaza-Egypt border in 2025, co-released a report accusing Israel of planning to ethnically cleanse the territory. In September, the senator led an unsuccessful resolution to force the state department to issue a report on violence in the West Bank.

Schumer’s criticism of Israel has been comparatively muted – he did not vote for the efforts to cute off arm sales, but did support Van Hollen’s resolution on the state department report. When he was majority leader in 2024, and thereby the highest-ranking Jewish official in the US government, Schumer called on the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, to step aside.

Last week’s sweep of the midterm elections seems to vindicate his leadership of Senate Democrats – after all, the party won just about every state it was contesting, and some where it had invested few resources. Yet Van Hollen said Schumer could have done better, noting that several candidates he had backed in the primaries wound up being rejected by voters.

After the election, reports emerged that Van Hollen was not planning to challenge Schumer, fueling speculation that he would instead run for president in 2028. He now says he’s not interested in a presidential run, and announced the bid for party leader just as activists again called for Senate Democrats to replace Schumer.

“Our members are tired of politicians content with incrementalism – they want bold, creative leadership that will help Democrats usher in affordability and accountability without delay or compromise in the next Congress,” said Joel Payne, the executive director of liberal group MoveOn.
“We welcome and will support any potential Senate leader willing to meet the moment.”

A small number of Democratic senators have publicly backed Van Hollen since he announced his leadership bid, including Bernie Sanders, the independent progressive who caucuses with the party, and incoming senators Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan and Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota. Others, such as Elissa Slotkin of Michigan, incoming senator Adam Hamilton of Kansas and Juliana Stratton of Illinois, said the party should choose a new leader, but have not said who that should be.

Schumer, meanwhile, retains considerable sway in the party, and has been endorsed by progressive and moderate senators alike. Those who have backed him argue he’s been effective, and point to last week’s results as proof.
“Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series?” asked Angus King, the Maine independent who caucuses with the Democrats, and endorsed Schumer.

articles.title: Tanker collides with cruise ship on Mississippi in New Orleans
articles.summary: A freighter collided with a cruise ship carrying around 130 people in New Orleans, causing the paddlewheel vessel to capsize. More than 30 people were hospitalized but all passengers have been…

image.caption: At least 180 people were rescued from the ship after it was hit and capsized on FridayImage: Enan Chediak/The Advocate/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: More than 30 people were hospitalized but no deaths were reported after a freighter collided with a cruise ship on the Mississippi River in the US on Friday.

Authorities said at least 180 passengers and crew were rescued. New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno described it as "a miracle on the Mississippi," adding that none of those hospitalized had critical injuries.
Footage showed the paddlewheel cruise boat capsizing following the impact with the much larger cargo vessel and rescue teams rushing to get people in life jackets out of the water.
'It was just chaos'
The accident happened near the port of New Orleans when the freighter Atlantic Asphalt hit the cruise ship while it was docked.
"It was just chaos," local witness Devon Flanagan was quoted by news agency AP.

"You had all types of ships, like other barges and other companies down there trying to help out, which also was a little convoluted because you had people still in the water," he described the scene.
The company operating the passenger ship, American Cruise Lines, said in a statement that "guests and crew were evacuated, and we are deeply concerned for everyone involved."

blocks.caption: The collision happened in the busy port area of New OrleansImage: Enan Chediak/The Advocate/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: According to AP, the cruise ship was built in 2015, is five stories tall and can hold up to 150 passengers. It was finishing an eight-day cruise to several Mississippi River destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi.
When news of the collision broke, it was long initially unclear whether there were any fatalities and how many people were injured or missing.

Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry said he was on his way to New Orleans. "We are aware of the incident on the Mississippi and we are in close contact with local officials and law enforcement," he wrote on X.

US Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin wrote on social media that "we are throwing every asset we have to helping rescue missing passengers" and that his department was coordinating closely with state officials.

articles.title: U.S. Treasury Secretary frustrated by Commerce Department's inaction on Nvidia chips
articles.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday he was frustrated with the Commerce Department's delay in placing restrictions on Nvidia chip exports to a company led by an alleged Chinese spy.

image.caption: U.S. Treasury Scott Bessent, seen in a photo taken in the Oval Office last month, says he's frustrated with the U.S. Commerce Department's delay in placing restrictions on Nvidia chip exports to a company led by an alleged Chinese spy. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

blocks.text: World·New
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday he was frustrated with the Commerce Department's delay in placing restrictions on Nvidia chip exports to a company led by an alleged Chinese spy.
Bessent supports adding Megaspeed International to export control list

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday he was frustrated with the U.S. Commerce Department's delay in placing restrictions on Nvidia chip exports to a company led by an alleged Chinese spy.

Bessent said on CNBC that his department, along with the U.S. departments of State and Defence and the U.S. trade representative, were in favour of adding Singapore-based Megaspeed International to an export control list for months but that the Commerce Department was in charge of the matter.
"Commerce has the pen, and you will have to ask them about their internal processes," Bessent said. "My deputy has been pushing this for months."

Bessent's comments were an unusually public rebuke of a fellow cabinet member, in this case U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. Commerce oversees U.S. government controls over exports of sensitive, high-tech goods.
Trump's Commerce Department under fire as Nvidia CEO scandal continues to rock markets

The comments come as Nvidia's ties to Megaspeed play a prominent role in the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Huang allegedly had an affair with the CEO of Megaspeed, Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence suspects is a Chinese spy, the New York Times has reported. China has denied allegations of spying.

Lutnick has come under increasing scrutiny because of his reportedly close relationship with Jensen Huang. The ex-Nvidia CEO is also close to U.S. President Donald Trump and visited the White House on Sept. 29 to discuss AI safety.

items: What the Jensen Huang scandal means for Trump and his administration
The Nvidia scandal has wiped away $1T in value. What that means for your investments

blocks.text: The Times reported Thursday that Lutnick resisted placing greater limits on the sale of Nvidia's more advanced chips to China. Chinese firms have accessed Nvidia's chips through companies like Megaspeed, which has reportedly purchased more than $4 billion US worth of Nvidia's advanced semiconductors.

The split in Trump's cabinet reflects the widespread fallout from the scandal that has engulfed Nvidia, one of the most valuable publicly traded companies in the world. Nvidia's computer chips play a central role in the buildout of artificial intelligence, powering AI models such as those developed by OpenAI and Anthropic.
U.S. interest in restricting chip sales

The U.S. government has, since the Biden administration, sought to restrict the sale of the most advanced AI computer chips to China in an effort to protect U.S. technology companies' lead. Yet China has at times retaliated, creating controversy over how far the U.S. should push its restrictions.
The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to messages seeking comment.
Bessent declined to comment Friday on the Times report that he confronted Lutnick last week in the White House's situation room about Megaspeed.
Separately, Axios reported this week that Lutnick received a classified memo this spring warning about Jensen Huang's relationship with a suspected spy.

items: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after affair raises national security concerns
How China gets around the U.S. ban on Nvidia chips

blocks.text: Last year, Megaspeed was accused of illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China, but in December the company said there was "no evidence" of such exports.
The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security began investigating Megaspeed International in 2024. The bureau later handed off the investigation to the U.S. Justice Department.
Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO
A person familiar with the bureau's investigation denied any intervention from Nvidia. The person wasn't authorized to discuss the matter publicly and spoke on condition of anonymity.

The Justice Department's national security division is investigating whether Megaspeed violated export control laws in an inquiry that will also include scrutiny of Alice Huang, according to a person familiar with the matter, The Associated Press reported Wednesday.

On Thursday, Megaspeed maintained it takes its obligation to comply with American export control laws "extremely seriously" — and that it was committed to working "constructively and transparently" with the U.S. government.
Numerous members of Congress have said they will investigate Lutnick's actions and called for him to testify on Capitol Hill.
Democrats demand Lutnick preserve records

On Thursday, Oregon Sen. Ron Wyden and Massachusetts Rep. Richard Neal, both Democrats, wrote Lutnick a letter demanding that he preserve all records related to decisions about Nvidia chip exports, pending an investigation. Wyden and Neal are the top Democrats on the Senate finance and House ways and means committees, respectively.

U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has received a letter from two Democrats demanding he preserve all records related to decisions about Nvidia chip exports, pending an investigation. (Alex Brandon/The Associated Press)

Trump's approval of advanced Nvidia chip exports to China "raises critical questions about whether and to what extent political considerations are improperly influencing policy decisions made by the Administration," Wyden and Neal wrote.
And the chair of the U.S. House foreign relations committee wants Nvidia's general counsel and a senior Commerce Department official to appear before Congress.

Rep. Brian Mast, a Republican from Florida, sent a letter this week to Jeff Kessler, undersecretary of commerce for industry and security, seeking a Dec. 2 hearing on computer chip smuggling and "reported interference by private companies into export control policies and enforcement investigations."
Mast also wants Nvidia chief counsel Tim Teter to appear the same day for a closed-door interview.

items: Nvidia and CEO Jensen Huang face lawsuit over handling of ties to alleged Chinese spy
Who is Alice Huang? Alleged Chinese spy, businesswoman involved with Nvidia CEO

blocks.text: Republican Sen. John Kennedy of Louisiana, a member of the Senate banking committee, urged Lutnick to hold a press conference to explain what he knew.

"The Commerce Department greenlit $4 billion of sales of advanced chips to the company of the spy that Mr. Huang was having an affair with and I want to know why," Kennedy said. "I want to know why the Commerce Department did it in light of the export controls, and everything I read indicates that this was a decision by the secretary himself."
Kennedy added that Lutnick should testify before the Senate and should be subpoenaed if necessary.

articles.title: Microsoft 'deeply sorry' for global outage after almost 24 hours of disruption
articles.summary: Experts say the event is a "stark reminder" of how heavily the world relies on a small group of big tech providers.

blocks.text: Microsoft has said it is "deeply sorry" for the service outage to its products, including Outlook and Teams, which has caused disruption around the world.

Services were broadly recovering by Friday afternoon, nearly 24 hours after issues began. Microsoft said it was making "encouraging progress", but added it does not know when services will fully recover.
The outage hit more than 70 countries, disrupting everything from business operations to government services and personal users. More than 430 million people use the affected products worldwide.
Microsoft said it was a technical issue introduced during a "network capacity upgrade" and not related to cyber or artificial intelligence agents.
Experts said the event was a "stark reminder" of how heavily businesses and vital services rely on a small group of big tech providers.
Users began reporting they were having trouble accessing Microsoft 365 products on Thursday.

By Friday, the far-reaching issue was affecting institutions from the Japanese government and the Philippines Supreme Court to the Australian spy agency, and trains, hospitals and courts in North America.
In the UK, some parts of the NHS, including GPs and hospitals, were affected, as were some schools and police forces.
UK cyber minister Liz Lloyd said the incident had "limited" impact on critical frontline services such as 999 calls, and there had been no disruption to the transport network.
In Canada, however, the national rail network said passengers may not be able to receive email updates about their trips, and hospitals across the country also had issues with emails.
In the US, staff members from the House of Representatives told Politico it had set back an entire day of legislative work as everything was on Microsoft's Outlook.
Singapore's government acknowledged some of its systems had been impacted, and in India, the outage disrupted work for many on Friday.
In Turkey, advisers and officials attending the COP31 climate summit in Antalya were left frustrated by being unable to access Outlook.
The issues also affected smaller businesses and individuals.

Microsoft first acknowledged users in the Americas were unable to access Exchange Online mailboxes at 17:54 GMT on Thursday, and shortly after warned the disruption was possibly affecting Microsoft 365 globally.
While it launched an investigation and engineers began working to restore services, by 04:36 on Friday Microsoft was reporting only a "partial recovery" in some parts of the world.
By 13:32, the tech giant said there were "broader improvements" in North America, "sustained improvements" across much of Europe and "encouraging recovery signals" in the Asia Pacific region.
Microsoft said it restored services gradually due to the scale of the problem and to help ensure services remain stable once they are up and running again.
"We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners," a Microsoft spokesperson said.
"We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously."
Microsoft said it has no "ETA" for when services will be fully recovered.
A full post-incident report will be released once Microsoft has completed a review.
Experts said while workers may have been happy to not have email access for the day, the incident showed the dependence many organisations have on these cloud-based services.
"The global Microsoft outage is a stark reminder of how heavily we rely on a handful of big tech providers," said Rob Demain, chief executive of cybersecurity firm e2e-assure.
Matt Saunders, field chief technology officer at tech consultancy Adaptavist, said it would be challenging to mitigate against a similar problem.
"Classic IT disaster planning strategies suggest using a second service for resilience, but in practice, it's almost impossible for a business to function without tools such as Microsoft," he said.
"In the wake of this outage, organisations must have a plan in place for how to work without such tools, for when incidents like this occur."

articles.title: Rescue underway in New Orleans after tanker hits river cruise boat
articles.summary: A tanker struck a cruise boat with 129 passengers on board in New Orleans on Friday, partially submerging the boat.

image.caption: Emergency personnel and crews respond after a tanker crashed into a river cruise boat in New Orleans on Friday. (Enan Chediak/The Advocate/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New
A tanker struck a cruise boat with 129 passengers on board in New Orleans on Friday, partially submerging the boat.
People in life-jackets seen in Mississippi River as emergency crews respond
Rescues were underway on the Mississippi River, officials said. Authorities did not immediately release whether there were injuries or deaths.
Video from the scene showed the much larger Atlantic Asphalt tanker hit the paddlewheel river boat while it appeared to be docked.

People were seen in the river in life-jackets or standing near the boat's railing as the other side of the American Heritage paddlewheeler listed further into the water. Other footage showed people being pulled from the water and debris, including deck chairs, floating in the river.

articles.title: US air force responds to suspected drone activity at RAF Lakenheath
articles.summary:
No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure at Suffolk site affected, says US military

The US air force has said it responded to “suspected unauthorised drone activity” on Friday night at an…

blocks.text: The US air force has said it responded to “suspected unauthorised drone activity” on Friday night at an airbase in the east of England.
No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected, the air force said.
Sirens were heard at RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk, one of several airbases in the UK used by the US military.

The force added: “We continue to work closely with our host nation counterparts to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, US and host nation civilians, contractors and all of our families.
“Protecting our shared community is a joint responsibility, and we encourage everyone to support this effort by reporting any unusual or suspicious activity to local authorities.”
The MP for West Suffolk, Nick Timothy, said the authorities at the base had told him “there is no threat to the public, and the incident is now resolved”.
He added: “Given the raised threat level, I continue to encourage everyone to report anything suspicious or out of the ordinary to the authorities.”
More details soon …

articles.title: Probation officers in England and Wales vote for strike action over pay and workloads
articles.summary:
Move deals blow to government’s plans to release thousands of prisoners early to tackle prison overcrowding

The government’s plans to release thousands of prisoners early were dealt a blow…

blocks.text: The government’s plans to release thousands of prisoners early were dealt a blow on Friday after probation officers across England and Wales voted to strike over pay and excessive workloads.

Members of the union, Napo, backed overtime restrictions and other forms of action short of a strike, which is likely to start on 23 November. Plans are being made for strike action to follow at a later stage.
The union, whose members work across probation offices and in family courts, said it launched its ballot because of an “inadequate” 5% pay offer from ministers and a failure to cut workloads.
Probation officers have come under increasing pressure since the launch of the latest early release scheme in October, which is meant to ease overcrowding in prisons.

They are responsible for monitoring offenders’ behaviour, overseeing their rehabilitation, monitoring their electronic tags and recalling them to prison for any offences or licence breaches, such as entering an exclusion or restriction zone protecting victims.
By the end of the year, about 2,500 offenders, some of whom are sex offenders, domestic abusers and stalkers, will be released under the scheme.

The union had sought a 12% increase. Napo general secretary Ian Lawrence said: “The high turnout by our members and the result vindicates the campaign to achieve a pay rise to make up lost ground in comparative pay with other staff employed within HMPPS [HM Prison and Probation Service].
“The vote also reflects serious anger at the state of probation workloads, which were already in crisis before the latest version of the prisoner early release scheme.”
Napo said probation wages have “stagnated” since 2010, with reception staff on a salary just above the minimum wage – the lowest in the civil service.

On pay, Napo members voted by 85% in favour of action short of strike action and 74% in favour of strike action. In a ballot on workloads, the vote was 87% in favour of action short of strike action and 75% in favour of strikes.
The Ministry of Justice is recruiting an additional 1,300 trainee probation officers for the 2026-27 financial year as part of a £700m investment package extending through 2028-29.
after newsletter promotion
The Institute for Government said slow progress on recruitment means probation practitioners were still overstretched and ill-equipped to absorb additional demand.

It said there had been a serious staff shortage in probation for several years, with the number of probation officers consistently 25-30% below target staffing. As of March 2026, nine probation delivery units (8% of the total) had a vacancy rate of 40% or more.

A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said: “Probation staff do a vital job protecting the public, which is why we have put a strong offer on the table, giving every worker a further 5% pay rise, which follows the biggest probation pay increase in over a decade alongside record investment. We’re also recruiting an additional 1,300 officers to significantly cut workloads.

“While we are disappointed that some have voted against this competitive deal, it will not change our first responsibility of protecting the public and we have robust contingency plans in place to ensure offenders are still subject to the same rigorous supervision.”

articles.title: Russia is ‘setting traps’ in Ukraine talks, EU foreign policy chief warns
articles.summary:
Kaja Kallas says Moscow is trying to divert attention from its aggression by raising issue of European security

The EU’s foreign policy chief has warned against “walking into the traps that…

blocks.text: The EU’s foreign policy chief has warned against “walking into the traps that Russia is setting” as she said Moscow was trying to start a debate about European security in order to divert attention from its aggression.

“We have one aggressor and one victim, and the aggressor does not have security concerns,” Kaja Kallas said on arrival at an EU leaders’ summit in Dublin. “Nobody has ever attacked them. They have attacked others. I mean, keep the focus, people.”

In talks on the Ukraine war, Russia has revived its hardline demands for a total overhaul of European security – demands that were rejected in 2021 because they were seen as an infringement of the sovereignty of central and eastern European countries. The latest round of talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US was held this week in Abu Dhabi.

Donald Trump’s envoy and son-in-law, Jared Kushner, said on Thursday night that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to expand the next round of peace negotiations to include the Europeans. However, Russia quickly contradicted that assurance.

European leaders have long said they will support Ukraine in any peace talks, but want to see a ceasefire before negotiations. They also stress the continent has an extensive web of security agreements that Russia has violated.

Friedrich Merz, the German chancellor, said: “Russia wants to talk about questions of a European security architecture. We do not need to discuss that; it already exists.” He added that it was a “given” that his country would be part of any European delegation.
The European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, said it was “self-explanatory that Europe is included in the peace talks to safeguard our interests, but also to support Ukraine”.

The Kremlin said on Friday: “Once we understand [Europe’s] real intentions and their willingness to contribute to the peace process, then we can make a decision on holding talks in an expanded format.” Russia’s lead negotiator in Abu Dhabi, Vladimir Medinsky, said it was “unclear what there is to discuss” with Europe.
The US call to involve Europe in talks has turned the spotlight on who would represent it.

Speaking after a summit of EU leaders in Dublin on Friday, the European Council president António Costa said leaders had agreed on a negotiating team: the EU institutions and E5 countries, namely Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland.
“Europe must speak with one clear and united voice in all discussions that shape the future of Ukraine and the security of our continent,” he said. “This is ultimately a team effort.”

The format had already emerged in recent months, but the need to formalise the grouping gained momentum after Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, this week urged his European allies to decide who will represent Europe in negotiations.

Kushner also mocked the absence of a single person to speak for the entire continent. “If Europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the Russians to include them in the negotiations,” he said earlier this week.
after newsletter promotion

But there was an increasingly settled view that Europe would not be represented by a single person, but by different interlocutors from the wider continent. Paris and Berlin had argued for a continued role for their own envoys in the E3 format of Britain, France and Germany, alongside EU representatives. Smaller member states put the emphasis more firmly on the EU representatives: Costa and Kallas, the EU’s high representative for foreign affairs and security policy.
Earlier in the day, Sweden’s prime minister, Ulf Kristersson, said the discussion on who should represent Europe was “slightly overstated” as it had differing interests.

Some of the issues in peace talks were “pure EU interests”, he said, citing financing Kyiv and Ukraine’s future membership in the bloc. He also supported other formats, such as the “pretty uncomplicated” E3 and the “very legitimate” E5, which includes Italy and Poland, as well as a role for EU representatives. He said: “I am quite flexible on that. I think what we actually say is more important than the exact configuration of the people in the room.”

Several at the summit, including Kallas, also pointed to the importance of including the UK, a founder member of the coalition of the willing, a broad group of countries committed to future peacekeeping in Ukraine.
Ireland’s taoiseach, Micheál Martin, said the UK and Norway each had a significant role and “that all has to be taken into consideration because it’s a European, continent-wide issue”.

The British prime minister, Andy Burnham, said it was for the EU to decide who would represent the bloc. He said there was a strong view among European leaders that it was for Europe – in the wider sense – “to decide its own arrangements” on security.

articles.title: Alberta announces royalty program as part of plan to double oilsands production
articles.summary: The province says the OGP is designed to lower upfront financial barriers to new projects and expansions, particularly as proponents of the Pacific Link pipeline look for companies to fill upcoming…

image.caption: Suncor Energy's Base Plant operation north of Fort McMurray, Alta., is shown in this photo from September. A new royalty program from the Alberta government aims to kickstart new development in the oilsands. (Bob Grieve/CBC)

blocks.text: Edmonton·New

The province says the OGP is designed to lower upfront financial barriers to new projects and expansions, particularly as proponents of the Pacific Link pipeline look for companies to fill upcoming capacity.
The Oil Sands Growth Program offers a two per cent royalty rate for five years

The Alberta government is introducing a royalty incentive program it says will help with the province's plans to double current oilsands production goal by 2035 by easing the capital investment needed to kickstart new developments.
The Oil Sands Growth Program (OGP) announced Friday offers a steady 10-year royalty framework for new and expanding oilsands projects.

The program gives approved projects a reduced two per cent royalty rate during their first five years of production. The rates then increase by one percentage point annually until reaching six per cent during the ninth and tenth years.
“Oilsands projects require significant upfront capital and long-term certainty,” Brian Jean, Alberta’s energy and minerals minister, said in a Friday statement.

“By providing a predictable royalty framework during the critical early years of eligible projects, the Oil Sands Growth Program will help companies turn investment decisions into a new windfall for Albertans.”
The OGP does not replace the existing royalty program, according to a statement from the Alberta government.

The statement also added that does not guarantee a project’s approval or sidestep environmental or Indigenous consultation requirements; that eligibility will not be limited to the five members of the Oil Sands Alliance; and that approvals will be done on a project-by-project basis and can include expansions.

According to the government, existing oilsands projects will not be eligible for the OGP, and companies will return to the regular royalty regime after 10 years or if they cannot meet production, environmental or regulatory requirements.

The Alberta government plans to launch the OGP this spring, but says qualifying projects announced after Nov. 15 will still be eligible. The province will review the program’s effectiveness in December 2029.

“Today’s announcement is a positive step toward creating a globally competitive fiscal and regulatory environment in Alberta that attracts and incentivizes capital investment for growth in the oil sector that will benefit Albertans and Canadians for decades to come,” said Rich Kruger, CEO of Suncor Energy, in a statement.
The province expects the program to create tens of thousands of jobs and deliver billions of dollars in property taxes to rural municipalities.

Premier Danielle Smith has said she wants oilsands production to double to eight million barrels per day by 2035. A provincial statement released Friday predicts doubling output could generate roughly $205 billion in cumulative additional revenues by 2040 and more than $1.3 trillion by 2060.

“Alberta has the resources, the expertise and the ambition to remain a global energy leader. The Oil Sands Growth Program will make the province even more attractive for investment, help get new oil sands projects moving and grow production for the long term,” said Smith in a statement.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Vincent McDermott covers Fort McMurray and the Wood Buffalo region for CBC News. He was previously the editor of Fort McMurray Today, where he was part of a team that won a National Newspaper Award for coverage of the 2016 Horse River Wildfire. He is also a former contributor to the official magazine of the Royal Astronomical Society of Canada. He can be reached at vincent.mcdermott@cbc.ca

articles.title: Tanker collides with river cruise ship carrying more than 130 people in New Orleans – latest updates
articles.summary: Rescue efforts under way as ship takes on water; governor confirms incident in Mississippi River

blocks.text: Photos are circulating on social media of people climbing out and onto the balconies of the ship that is now turned completely on its side.

Local media is reporting that multiple people have already been rescued, and helicopters were seen in the air along with ambulances waiting nearby. Several people can be seen in the river wearing life jackets.

Videos circulating across social media appear to show the moment the Atlantic Asphalt tanker crashes into the side of the American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage while the cruise ship is docked on the Mississippi River. The ship then falls to its side towards the open water and begins sinking rapidly.
Ramon Antonio Vargas
An emergency response source said that there were efforts underway to rescue people from the water. That source said it was possible the tanker had lost power before striking the American Heritage.
Images on social media showed the American Heritage on its side. It was docked on the Mississippi River outside the port of New Orleans’s administrative building when it was hit.
A tanker has collided with a river cruise liner carrying more than 130 people in New Orleans, authorities have said.
The governor of Louisiana has confirmed an incident in the Mississippi river. Jeff Landry said on X he was in contact with local officials and law enforcement.
The cruise liner was taking on water, local media reports said, and rescue efforts are under way.
The Port of New Orleans press secretary said the tanker collided with the American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage around 12:30 pm local time on Friday.
There were about 129 passengers onboard as well as crew, Port authorities told local media.
This is breaking news story. We’ll bring you the latest updates as we get them.

articles.title: SpaceX to attempt double catch of huge Starship rocket
articles.summary: Elon Musk’s company will try to grab both parts of the rocket for the first time.

blocks.text: The 124m-tall rocket is scheduled to blast off from the Starbase launchpad in Texas at 1645 local time (2245 GMT) with a 75-minute-long launch window.
After six and a half minutes, the first planned catch will be attempted when the bottom part of the rocket - the Super Heavy booster - returns to the launch tower.

The top part of the rocket, called the Ship, will continue its journey to space and deploy 26 satellites. These will form part of the Starlink constellation that provides high speed internet from space.
The Ship is then due to complete 14 orbits around the Earth before returning for the second catch attempt about 22 and a half hours after taking off.
Until now, SpaceX has managed to catch the Super Heavy Booster on three earlier test flights.
But the upper stage of the rocket, which only reached orbit for the first time in September, has never been grabbed by the chopsticks. Instead it's splashed down in the ocean.
SpaceX said it would only decide to try to catch the Ship after carefully assessing the vehicle while it's in space.
If any problems are detected there are various points during the flight when the rocket stage can be brought down in the ocean.
After SpaceX went public earlier this year, its shareholders will be carefully monitoring this flight, as will the US Space Agency.
The progress of Starship has direct implications for Nasa's attempt to land humans on the Moon in 2028 - a highly ambitious timeline.
SpaceX has been given a Nasa contract to configure the Ship into a lander that will eventually take astronauts down to the lunar surface.

But it's not the only company working with the US Space Agency. Blue Origin, owned by rival tech billionaire Jeff Bezos, also has a contract to use its New Glenn rocket and lander for the Moon touch down.
Both companies will also play a key role in Artemis III, which is currently planned for summer 2027- another challenging schedule.
This mission will see four astronauts in Nasa's Orion spacecraft attempt to dock with both SpaceX and Blue Origin's landers.
Starship will need to make a lot of progress in the coming months to meet these commitments - the pace of the rocket's development has been far slower than SpaceX had intended.
But Blue Origin also has much work to do. The company suffered a major setback earlier this year when its rocket exploded, totally destroying its launchpad in Florida.
Blue Origin had said they would be back in action by the end of this year, but a return to flight has now been delayed to early in 2027.

Nasa is under pressure to meet its timelines. Its administrator Jared Isaacman has said America is in a race with China to get to the Moon. China plans to land its Taikonauts on the lunar surface by 2030.

articles.title: Tanker collides with cruise ship on Mississippi River in New Orleans
articles.summary:

A tanker collided with an overnight cruise ship on the Mississippi River in

blocks.text: A tanker collided with an overnight cruise ship on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday afternoon, prompting a large emergency response, according to officials.

Images on social media showed the American Heritage on its side. It was docked on the Mississippi River outside the port of New Orleans’s administrative building when it was hit.
More details soon …

articles.summary: Germany, France, the UK, Italy and Poland — as well as the EU itself — will jointly represent Europe in possible peace talks. Meanwhile, a second car bomb in two days has exploded in Moscow. DW has…
