articles.title: How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House
articles.summary: Jensen Huang's personal life may have triggered the crisis, but the questions now reach into the White House itself.

blocks.text: How close is Donald Trump to Jensen Huang?
The answer is very.

The Nvidia boss was one of the few business leaders with direct access to the US president. He had met Trump repeatedly, travelled with him to Britain and, in May, joined him on Air Force One for his trip to China.

Jensen Huang wasn't just another tech billionaire seeking the president's ear. He had become an important voice in one of the biggest arguments inside the administration: how much of America's most advanced technology should be allowed to reach China.

Nvidia makes the chips that power the AI revolution. Washington has restricted exports of its most advanced processors to China since 2022, believing they could help Beijing develop its military and technological capabilities.

But enforcing those restrictions is difficult. Chips can be bought legally by customers in countries such as Singapore and Malaysia and then diverted to China. Chinese companies can also rent access to computing power through data centres outside the country.

Jensen Huang has long argued that the restrictions are counterproductive. They shut Nvidia out of a huge market and encourage Chinese companies to develop their own alternatives. Trump appeared sympathetic to this view, allowing Nvidia to resume sales of certain chips to China last year in return for a share of the revenue, although its most advanced Blackwell chips remain off limits.
But that relationship now looks rather more complicated.

The allegations surrounding Jensen Huang's reported affair with Alice Huang, of no relation but a former executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed, have raised the possibility that a foreign intelligence operation was targeting not just a powerful businessman, but someone with unusually close access to the American president.

US intelligence reportedly suspects Alice Huang of having links to Chinese intelligence. Beijing has rejected the allegations. Nvidia's board says it has no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised. But the affair has opened up a much bigger question: what did the administration in Washington know, and what did it do about it?
That question leads directly to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

His department was responsible for controlling exports of sensitive American technology. It was also being pressed to act on concerns about Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China.

On Thursday, Megaspeed chief executive, Tan Yong Pong, also known as James Tan, said the company "takes its compliance obligations under US export control laws extremely seriously" and is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government". He said the company had co-operated with US Commerce Department inspections.
A highly classified memo was shared with Lutnick about the concerns surrounding Alice Huang and Megaspeed. He resisted taking action against the company, a decision that is now under scrutiny.
Other senior officials wanted a tougher response. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was among those who reportedly questioned why Megaspeed had not been placed on the Commerce Department's blacklist.

There were also questions about why an investigation into the Singapore-based company was stopped after Nvidia intervened. The New York Times reported that Nvidia's general counsel contacted Commerce Department investigators probing suspected chip smuggling by Megaspeed invoking a senior Trump appointee. The department allegedly then froze its investigation and handed the case to the Justice Department.

This apparently highlighted a significant disagreement about the direction of Trump's China policy. Huang wanted access to the Chinese market. Other officials were supposedly worried about the national security consequences. Lutnick was caught in the middle.
Now the political pressure is building.

Members of Congress from both parties want answers. Democrats have launched an investigation into how the Commerce Department vetted Chinese companies approved to buy AI chips. Republicans are also questioning the administration's approach.
And Jensen Huang's departure has not eased the pressure.

Republican representative John Moolenaar, who chairs the House Select Committee on China, said it was in the national interest for Nvidia and other American AI firms to succeed, but that companies "should never jeopardise our nation's security" by giving Chinese firms access to their most advanced chips.

Senator Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, said Huang's resignation did not absolve him of responsibility, and urged Lutnick to explain why export control loopholes remain open.
Meanwhile Jensen Huang's team told Republican lawmakers on Wednesday that he plans to cooperate with their request to testify behind closed doors.
The White House has not responded to the BBC's request for comment.
It has, however, told the New York Post that Trump has complete confidence in Lutnick, describing him as "the most transformative commerce secretary in modern history".
That is a fairly emphatic show of support, particularly amid reports that officials are weighing whether Lutnick should be forced out.

There are some obvious questions. If Lutnick had indeed been warned about the risks, why did his department fail to act? And if other senior officials were indeed pressing for action, why did it take so long?
The BBC has contacted the Commerce Department for comment. But there is an even bigger question for Trump.

The president cultivated a close relationship with Huang. He was directly involved in decisions about chip sales to China. And, according to reporting in the New York Times, he was briefed on the intelligence concerns.
This is becoming difficult to dismiss as the misjudgement of one businessman or one government department.

Jensen Huang's personal life may have triggered the crisis, but the questions now reach into the White House itself. How much influence did he have? What did the president know? And who was ultimately responsible for protecting America's most sensitive technology?

articles.title: Sandiganbayan declares Zaldy Co’s 3 co-accused as fugitives
articles.summary: The three are facing graft and malversation charges over alleged irregularities in the procurement and construction of a P289.4-million flood control project in Naujan, Oriental Mindoro

blocks.text: ANTI-GRAFT COURT. The Sandiganbayan in Quezon City.
Jansen Romero/Rappler
The three are facing graft and malversation charges over alleged irregularities in the procurement and construction of a P289.4-million flood control project in Naujan, Oriental Mindoro
MANILA, Philippines – The Sandiganbayan Fifth Division has declared three co-accused of dismissed Ako Bicol representative Zaldy Co as fugitives.

In its ruling on Tuesday, November 10, the anti-graft court named Sunwest board members Anthony Ngo and Consuelo Aldon, and Department of Public Works and Highways Mimaropa materials engineer Timogen Sacar as fugitives. The court said they had demonstrated “an unmistakable intent to evade warrants and avoid prosecution.”

The three are facing graft and malversation charges over alleged irregularities in the procurement and construction of a P289.4-million flood control project in Naujan, Oriental Mindoro. The allegedly defective project was first exposed by Oriental Mindoro Governor Humerlito “Bonz” Dolor.

blocks.caption: Flood control anomalies: The case of Oriental Mindoro

blocks.text: According to prosecutors, the three remain at large despite the issuance of arrest warrants on November 21, 2025, nearly a year ago.

“Given the high-profile nature of the case, it is reasonable to conclude that the accused are aware of the criminal proceedings and the outstanding warrants issued against them. Thus, by staying beyond the reach of law enforcement while fully aware of pending warrants of arrest confirms accused’s deliberate intent to evade the judicial process,” the Sandiganbayan said.
Co, the beneficial owner of Sunwest, also remains at large despite facing multiple cases. He reportedly fled the country.
Sunwest was identified by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. as one of the top flood control contractors under his administration.
The Sandiganbayan also ordered the cancellation of the passports of Ngo, Aldon, and Sacar to prevent them from seeking refuge overseas.

“Removing the official travel document necessary for the fugitive to leave the country or to travel between foreign countries hinders the attempts to evade judicial process,” the court said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Iran says it destroyed US military radar in Bahrain in retaliatory strike
articles.summary:
First direct attack on US military installations for months was in response to US airstrike on communications tower

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it has targeted and…

blocks.text: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it has targeted and destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain – its first direct attack on US military installations for months – in response to a US airstrike on a communications tower in Sirik overlooking the strait of Hormuz.

“This is a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to end its aerial mischief and oil smuggling in the strait of Hormuz,” the IRGC said. “In the event of repeated violations and aggression, the IRGC aerospace force is on full alert to confront the enemy without constraint.”

Donald Trump has said in a series of media interviews over the past 24 hours that he will attack Iran only if necessary, claiming that Gulf countries such as Saudi Arabia have urged him to hold back from planned large-scale military strikes.
Trump announced that he had asked his vice-president, JD Vance, to end his interest in negotiating a new deal with Iran and instead focus on corruption and fraud in Democrat-run cities and states.

Vance had been seen by the Iranians as the most trustworthy figure close to Trump, but they had rejected his request for a personal meeting with their negotiators to discuss the terms of a peace deal.

Vance has been in the forefront of Republicans saying the war led to the massive Republican losses in the midterms. Trump said he had been disappointed in the American public, since higher diesel prices was a small price to pay for preventing Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon.

An opinion poll in the UK shows 65% of the British public would oppose the US resuming the war in Iran, and only 14% would back it. The poll was conducted by YouGov for the Council for Arab-British Understanding (Caabu).
It also found 54% oppose UK bases being used by the US to mount attacks on Iran, with 29% in favour. Support for additional UK sanctions against Iran was found to be 45%, with 22% opposed.

The poll was conducted on Tuesday and Wednesday this week, before two Iranians were found guilty on Thursday of spying and planning attacks on journalists in the UK. The Iranian embassy has rejected the court judgment as an attempt to advance a political agenda.

Chris Doyle, the director of Caabu, said: “The British public are sceptical about any war on Iran and what it might achieve. What might make the Burnham government take note is the very high level of opposition to any further war amongst 2024 Labour voters, at 79%.”

Iran’s Assembly of Experts, a body of elected Islamic jurists responsible for choosing the supreme leader, has become the first governing institution in Iran to call for a review of the country’s defence doctrine, potentially leading to religious permission for Iran to try to acquire a nuclear weapon.

In a statement released on Thursday, the assembly called for reviewing Iran’s membership of the nuclear non-proliferation treaty, describing the move as an “unavoidable necessity” and a “public and national demand”.

The intervention carries a religious as much as political significance because the 88-strong assembly comprises senior clerics, most of whom are supposed to be qualified to exercise independent Islamic legal reasoning.

Iran has had a longstanding prohibition on nuclear weapons, based on a fatwa issued by the late supreme leader Ali Khamenei, but the relevance of the fatwa in the wake of the US attacks on Iran has been questioned widely inside political and security circles.
Whether Iran has the stockpiles of uranium or technology to build a nuclear weapon is contested.

The UN nuclear inspectorate has expressed alarm about a continued lack of information from Iran about its nuclear sites. It said: “Our concerns are growing over Iran’s refusal to allow access to design information or inspections of the Isfahan facility. We do not know the exact location of the Isfahan uranium enrichment facility or whether it contains nuclear materials. It is imperative that we carry out our verification activities in Iran without further delay.”

articles.title: Ombudsman on Romualdez's P560-M cash inflow: Where did it come from?
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Friday asked about the source of the P560 million in money transfers to former Speaker and Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez from 2022 to 2025, if they didn't come from…

blocks.text: Published November 13, 2026 7:39pm

Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Friday asked about the source of the P560 million in money transfers to former Speaker and Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez from 2022 to 2025, if they didn't come from kickbacks related to flood control projects.

Remulla raised the question a day after Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) financial investigator Atty. Jan Mark Busa testified before Romualdez’s bail hearing that the P560.5 million worth of remittances were not related to flood control transactions.
Specifically, Busa said the remittances did not come from the Department of Public Works and Highways, any contractor, or then House Appropriations Panel Chair Zaldy Co.
Co is Romualdez’s co-accused in the P7.4 billion plunder case over his alleged involvement in the flood control kickback scheme.
“Saan nanggaling ‘yun? Saan nanggaling iyong pera? And AMLC is not necessarily the only one who knows where the money came from,” Remulla said.
(Where did that money come from?)
Asked if the AMLC witness's testimony affected the strength of the case against Romualdez, Remulla said, “Not at all.”
“Saka marami pa kaming testigo. Don’t worry about that,” he added.
(We still have other witnesses.)

Other co-accused of Romualdez and Co include Romualdez’s personal assistant Joselyn Tragua Sereño and Felicito Cristobal Guevarra, president of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corporation, over their alleged links to the flood control kickback scheme. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: Rosalía scoops historic third best album award at Latin Grammys
articles.summary: The Spanish singer is recognised for her fourth album Lux which was released last year to rave reviews.

blocks.text: Image source, EPA
Rosalía released her fourth album Lux last year to rave reviews
ByRiyah Collins
BBC Newsbeat
Spanish star Rosalía has made history as the first woman to win the best album award at the Latin Grammys three times, after being recognised for her project Lux.
The singer took home five trophies in total, including two for her track La Perla which was named song of the year and best pop song.
La Perla was also nominated for record of the year but missed out to Argentine singer Milo J's song Niño.

Rosalía released Lux last year to rave reviews and collecting her award at the ceremony in Las Vegas on Thursday, she said: "To all the people who told me I wasn't good enough, or that my music was too weird, I'm thankful I didn't listen."
The Barcelona-born artist then added: "Now I'm winning these prizes."
Rosalía, who opened the ceremony with a performance of some of her biggest songs, was honoured with the prize for best alternative music album.
She also picked up best shortform music video for her track Sauvignon Blanc.
The singer had previously won best album for El Mal Querer in 2019 and Motomami in 2022 - and her third Lux is also tipped to be a favourite when nominations are announced for the Grammys next week.

blocks.caption: Image caption, After a career spanning three decades, Daddy Yankee was recognised with a lifetime achievement award

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
After a career spanning three decades, Daddy Yankee was recognised with a lifetime achievement award
It was also a big night for Puerto Rican reggaeton legend Daddy Yankee, who won the person of the year award.
He performed some of his best-loved tracks including Gasolina and Con Calma, and was joined on stage by rappers including LL Cool J and French Montana.
Punjabi singer Diljit Dosanjh, who collabed with Daddy Yankee on Pokito, even took a break from his Aura India tour for the set, making him the first Indian artist to perform at the Latin Grammys.
Dosanjh superfan Devanshi Arora described the singer's appearance as "a cultural revolution".
"It's really invigorating and motivating to see someone from my country has made it all around the world," she tells Newsbeat.
She sees a lot of similarities between South American and Punjabi communities and hopes this leads to more collaborations - with a link-up between Dosanjh and Bad Bunny top of her wishlist.
Daddy Yankee was presented with the lifetime achievement award by Janet Jackson, who told him in Spanish that his music "has inspired an entire generation".

blocks.caption: Image caption, Diljit Dosanjh became the first Indian artist to perform at the Latin Grammys

blocks.text: Diljit Dosanjh became the first Indian artist to perform at the Latin Grammys
Accepting the prize for record of the year, Milo J seemed surprised to have won ahead of strong competition from Karol G, Jorge Drexler, Carin León as well as Rosalía.
The 20-year-old took home four trophies in the end and gave a shout out to Argentine folk music.
He described Niño as the song "I'm most proud of out of everything I've created so far".
"Long live Argentine folk music," he added.
Elsewhere, ARIA VEGA was named best new artist and songwriter of the year went to Sara Schell.
Additional reporting by Abu Bakar Yasin

articles.title: What’s behind Australia’s surge in teen extremism?
articles.summary:
Young people are being found with ‘hard drives full of what can only be described as gore’, one expert says

  • Get our

blocks.text: In March, Guardian Australia revealed that most people who have been charged with the new federal crime of possession of violent extremist material are under 18.
This week Australian federal police sounded the alarm about a surge in teen extremism: 32 of the 37 young people prosecuted in counter-terrorism cases since 2020 were charged in the past two years.

The growth in youth extremism is happening within a sprawling online ecosystem. My investigations have tracked the rise of online networks that urge violence and nihilism for their own sake, in which perpetrators coerce victims not much younger than themselves to commit brutal and degrading acts.

In a review of 55 youth terrorism cases, the AFP has found that the profile is mixed. They are often young men. Many have received some support or intervention for a mental health condition. Some are from stable homes, others not.
What they have most in common is that they are young people on the internet. Experts say the age of those caught up in these crimes is decreasing.
In the last month two teenagers in Darwin have been charged with collecting documents that could facilitate acts of terrorism.

The arrests came five months after another NT teenager was charged with making posts with “pro-Nazi, anti-immigration, anti-trans and white nationalist themes”. The charge sheet alleges he also possessed videos of white nationalist terrorist attacks, including the 2019 Christchurch mosque shooting and the 2022 Buffalo shooting that it partly inspired.
All matters are still before the courts.
Experts involved in harm prevention programs, including the Victoria University professor Debra Smith, have watched the age of this cohort decrease dramatically over the past decade.

Instead of considering the challenge exclusively through the lens of radicalisation, Smith says we need to recognise that some young people are being socialised and finding identity in online spaces that may appear exciting and transgressive but are ultimately harmful to themselves, and may encourage them to do harm to others.
She has seen cases where teenagers are being found with “hard drives full of what can only be described as gore”.

“It’s like getting involved in any other … unhealthy subcultural aspect of life … [such as] gangs or crime for payment,” she says. “There’s this offering of what young people can look at and get involved in that just simply wasn’t there years ago.”

The Guardian’s investigation into the growth of extremist material charges, as well as the surge of young people in Australia ensnared in sadistic online extortion and gore networks, reveals an amorphous online ecosystem in which young people may easily come into contact with extreme and violent content.

A teenager in New South Wales who pleaded guilty to possessing violent extremist material, among other charges, described how he first came across such content on TikTok when he was 14 and sought validation by talking to others online. He used ChatGPT to research the Boston marathon bomber Dzhokhar Tsarnaev as well as security arrangements at the Sydney Opera House. He was sentenced to a three-year community corrections order.
Others have told police how they became involved in so-called “gore” channels on Telegram, where more and more extreme footage – including of animal abuse – is traded.

Given the age of many involved, Levi West, a research fellow at the Australian National University, says they may be considered as much victims as perpetrators, which is a significant challenge for how authorities respond.
after newsletter promotion

It’s important for parents, schools and others to think about what’s sitting underneath the uptick in numbers, he says, and not just the “algorithms”. He points to the legacies of Covid-19 and lockdowns as well as the presence of screens and digital technologies in the lives of young people.
“We are not going to arrest our way out of this problem,” West says.
With people as young as 13 before the courts, Australia must consider if authorities are taking the right approach and have the right resources for this challenge.

The Guardian’s investigation into the possession of extremist material charges in South Australia and around the country found that many of those who had been before the courts faced a range of health and social difficulties, including autism diagnoses and learning challenges – and raised questions about whether some young people understand a crime has been committed.
Smith has seen many young people caught up in these activities who come from troubled family backgrounds, while others have had every opportunity in life.

There is a role for everyone involved in caring for young people, she says, from parents and schools to sporting clubs, to recognise when someone might be engaging in harmful behaviours long before there is a risk of violence, then help them access non-punitive pathways for help.
“It’s really important to understand it through a developmental lens – that these are young people who are making decisions with young brains,” Smith says.
“My grave concern is that if we are just giving everyone terrorism offences at [age] 12, 13, 14, 15, we’re starting to label them the thing that they will become.”

articles.title: Van Hollen takes aim at Schumer as Democrats face first big test after midterms – US politics live
articles.summary:
Senator Van Hollen says midterm results show Americans want change in Washington, and Democrats need new leadership to deliver that

Good morning, and welcome to the US politics live…

blocks.text: Key events

items: 21m agoVan Hollen takes aim at Schumer as Democrats face first big test after midterm wins

blocks.text: Van Hollen takes aim at Schumer as Democrats face first big test after midterm wins
Good morning, and welcome to the US politics live blog.
Barely a week after sweeping to a stunning midterm victory, Democrats have found themselves facing an altogether different battle, one within their own ranks.

Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen has launched a challenge to Chuck Schumer, of New York, for the Senate’s top Democratic leadership post. Announcing his decision during an interview with MS Now last night, Van Hollen argued that last week’s midterm election results showed Americans wanted a fundamental change in Washington, and that Democrats needed new leadership in order to deliver that.

blocks.caption: Chris Van Hollen said he is challenging Chuck Schumer to be Senate majority leader in the next Congress.  Photograph: Win McNamee/Getty Images

blocks.text: He said:

double quotation markWe saw a huge outburst of democracy on election day – red states, blue states, purple states – and it wasn’t only a rejection of Donald Trump and his corruption, his wars and his cruelty, it was also about a call for a larger change, to take on a broken economic system that’s rigged in favour of the very wealthy against working people, and it’s fuelled by a corrupt political system. The call was to reject the status quo and to reject business as usual, and to do that, I think we need new leadership.”

His challenge came just days after Democrats secured control of the Senate, winning at least 55 seats in what has been a remarkable election cycle for the party. Winning the leadership contest requires a majority of the caucus, about 28 or 29 senators, with an election scheduled for next month.
The caucus votes behind closed doors by secret ballot, but Van Hollen told MS Now that he had the support of “more than 10” Democratic senators.

Progressive heavyweight Bernie Sanders, an independent senator from Vermont who caucuses with the Democrats, has already publicly declared he will not support Schumer, saying “the time is now for change”. Endorsing Van Hollen, Sanders said: “The American people voted for change. They want a Democratic Party that will stand up to powerful special interests, take on the billionaire class and fight for working families.”
Incoming Democratic senator Abdul El-Sayed, of Michigan, has also openly backed Van Hollen, saying he was “proud to stand with him in his bid to lead our Senate majority”.

double quotation markThe American public spoke clearly last week. They rejected Trumpism. But we have yet to earn our mandate. That will require bold leadership. I called [Van Hollen] to lead our caucus as a candidate back in April because he leads with courage and experience. We need both right now.”

Responding to Van Hollen’s leadership bid, Schumer, who has led Senate Democrats since January 2017, said he welcomed “a discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead”, but that he had the votes to be re-elected as leader.

articles.title: House prosecutors dismiss Sara Duterte defense evidence as 'watusi,' not 'kwitis'
articles.summary: The House prosecution team on Friday said that the counter evidence presented by the defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte in her impeachment trial is not explosive and is only as good as a…

blocks.text: Published November 13, 2026 7:08pm

The House prosecution team on Friday said that the counter evidence presented by the defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte in her impeachment trial is not explosive and is only as good as a watusi or a small, friction-ignited firecracker that hardly makes noise.
House lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro of Batangas made the observation following the annoucement of the defense not to present 18 out of its initial 24 witnesses.

“In totality, 18 out of 24 witnesses were submitted by the defense to the impeachment court for the issuance of subpoenas, but they did not proceed to take the witness stand. Either the witness declined or stipulated (agreed) to the documents or testimony that was intended to be presented. And indeed, this is the first time that we are hearing the answer of the respondent vice president, and we were anticipating explosive testimonies and/or evidence,” Luistro said in a press conference.
“But apparently, hindi nga ito kwitis. Watusi pa yata ito,” Luistro added.
(But apparently, this isn't a rocket firework. It seems to be a watusi instead.)

Luistro said that the testimony of the six witnesses of the defense hardly accounted for the P817 million unexplained wealth that the prosecution is alleging based on analysis of the Vice President and her husband Manases Carpio’s bank account, bank transactions, tax filings and Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth conducted by expert witness and accountant-lawyer Alex Cabrera.
The defense witnesses include:

items: Davao City assessor Jaime Adalin
Davao City accountant Vingelin Bajan
Samal Island assessor Kenneth Enumerables
GenCorp. Industries Inc. counsel Suzette Punay
Lawyer Anel Antero, close friend of the Duterte-Carpio couple
Chad Parian, a friend of Carpio

blocks.text: “We were anticipating the defense to explain this huge amount of undeclared and/or unexplained property of the respondent Vice President. But the city assessor’s testimony concerned a property valued at P10 million," Luistro said.

"The testimony of the city assessor of Davao on a certain Davao property valued at P10 million, while the Samal assessor testified on the P4 million Samal property supposedly declared on the SALN… but they could not explain the disparity in the acquisition cost, the disparity in the technical description,” she said.

During the cross-examination of private prosecutors Mae Divinagracia and Lorna Kapunan on defense witnesses, it was also revealed that Davao City accountant Bajan was a former partner of the accounting firm of the declared businesses of the Duterte-Carpio couple. It was also bared that GenCorp Industries has paid the Vice President at least P2.1 million for return of capital even if the corporate records of the firm do not indicate that Duterte is a shareholder.

Defense panel spokesperson Michael Poa said they intend to present eight to 10 more witnesses after the impeachment trial break due to the country’s hosting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit and Related Summits from November 16 to 18.
Luistro, however, said they can only hope that the testimony of the next witness will directly respond to the prosecution’s allegations.

“We look forward to witnesses who will be able to testify on more substantial facts that are completely responsive to the specific allegations in the complaint: the failure to declare in the SALN, unexplained wealth, which means property cannot be supported by legal income. And three, non-divestment of other business and financial interests,” she said.

“As far as the prosecution is concerned, we have strongly and clearly established these three specific allegations, which to this date were ay hindi pa rin na ipaliwanag ng anim na testigo na iparinisenta ng defense,” Luistro added.
(The six witnesses have not been able to explain this.)
House prosecutor Joel Chua of Manila said the bloodbath that the Vice President earlier mentioned was happening to the defense.
“Naglabas po ng ebidensiya ang prosecution, nabugbog po sila. Naglabas ng ebidensiya, testigo ang defense, mas lalo pa silang nabugbog. Duguan na po sila,” Chua said.
(When we presented evidence, they ended up bloodied. When they presented theirs, they became more bloodied.)
“Hanggang ngayon, hindi pa tumatama iyong suntok nila sa prosecution,” Chua added.
(Until now, they have yet to land a punch on us.) —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Germany's Nmecha won't repeat controversial goal celebration
articles.summary: Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp says that midfielder Felix Nmecha will not repeat a goal celebration that sparked controversy over the past week. Germany are set to face Serbia and the Netherlands in…

image.caption: Felix Nmecha has made 14 appearances for GermanyImage: Tom Weller/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: With the controversy sparked by Felix Nmecha's celebrations after his goals in Dortmund's 2-1 win over Elfersberg last weekend, the subject was always going to be top of reporters' minds when Germany coach Jürgen Klopp faced reporters ahead of Friday's match against Serbia.
Nmecha celebrated the goals by mimicking taking a crown off his head and kneeling to place it on the ground.
This was understood by many to be a nod to a Ballers in God (BIG) campaign called "The King's Return."

BIG, a Christian group for footballers, has said it aims to "demonstrate love and respect towards everyone," but critics claim it discriminates against the queer and transexual people. The discourse generated by the celebration did not go unnoticed by the Germany boss.
Nmecha 'does not discriminate against anyone'
​Klopp told reporters in Belgrade on Thursday evening, that the 26-year-old Nmecha had assured him that he meant no harm by his actions.
"Last weekend I ​saw Felix score two great goals and saw the celebration and then the gesture. I thought nothing of it at the time, but then it all kicked off," he said.
"As the controversy escalated, I started looking into the details of the subject and trying to form a clear picture of it.

"I confronted him with all the things you (reporters) might have confronted him with. He told me that it had nothing to do with that at all, and that he loves all people and does not discriminate against anyone."
He then said that Nmecha had agreed not to repeat the celebration.

blocks.caption: Felix Nmecha's 'Crowns down' celebration caused much discussion over the past weekImage: Madeleine Fantini/HMB Media/picture alliance

blocks.text: Nations League quarterfinal berth up for grabs

In Friday's match, Klopp's goal will be to keep alive Germany's chances of reaching the Nations League quarterfinals with a win over Serbia. Germany are third in Group A2 with 5 points, trailing the Netherlands and Greece, who both have 8. Serbia, who Germany beat 2-0 in Munich last month, are still without a win.
"We feel well prepared," Klopp said, adding that his team were committed to earning "a final" for the last group last group game on Monday in Berlin against the Netherlands.

blocks.caption: Jürgen Klopp is hoping to keep alive Germany's chances of a Nations League quarterfinal berthImage: Michael Memmler/nordphoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: Just 5,000 children and coaches to attend

Klopp also expressed his disappointment that only a few thousand Serbian children would be admitted to the stadium due to a spectator ban. Originally, the game was to be played behind closed doors after Serbia was sanctioned for racist and discriminatory behavior by its fans. However, a clause in the UEFA rules allows a selected group of guests to attend. Now children under 15 accompanied by teachers or football coaches are expected to be at the match.
"We're expecting some 5,000 guests," a spokesman for the Serbian FA told the DPA news agency. The stadium's capacity is 55,000. The German FA has been allocated just 50 tickets for its fans.

articles.title: Guns, swords and pepper spray: Bishnoi-linked extortionists attacked in apparent retaliation
articles.summary: Documents obtained by CBC News reveal the existence of a previously unreported Bishnoi cell known as the Baweja group. Members have been tied to multiple shootings and extortion threats in Alberta…

image.caption: This image was pulled from the phone of an alleged extortionist who has been deported from Canada. It was disclosed to CBC News through Access to Information requests to the Immigration and Refugee Board. (CBC News)

blocks.text: On an afternoon in early October 2025, a van full of masked attackers pulled into the parking lot of a Calgary college and ambushed a group of young men caught napping in a white Mustang.
They pepper-sprayed one victim in the face. Police later found a baseball bat and sword at the scene.
The attackers even recorded the confrontation — sending a video to the parents of one victim, Kawanmeet Singh, to warn them about "what their son was doing and what behaviour he was engaging in."

According to documents obtained by CBC News, Singh was an alleged extortionist — leader of a previously unreported Bishnoi gang cell tied to multiple shootings, arsons and threats in Alberta and British Columbia.

items: 'We will rule in CANADA': Letter from Bishnoi gang to police disclosed to CBC News

blocks.text: 'Baweja gang' members identified
The attack on Singh and his associates is detailed in a trove of new Immigration and Refugee Board (IRB) documents disclosed to CBC News through a series of federal Access to Information requests.

IRB transcripts reveal both the existence of Singh's organization — known as the Baweja group — as well as new information from an insider about the Canadian operations of the larger transnational gang Lawrence Bishnoi has led from an Indian jail cell since 2015.

The confidential informant told police the gangsters are essentially laughing at the Canadian justice system, knowing the harshest penalty they're likely to face is deportation and a free ticket back to India.

One of a series of images taken from the phone of an alleged extortionist by police. This image is part of a trove of Immigration and Refugee Board documents released to CBC News through an Access to Information request. (CBC News)

Taken together, the documents provide insight into the inner workings of the linked extortion cells moving weapons, vehicles and people across Canada — as well as violence erupting on the periphery of the extortion networks.
Although public reports of extortion-related shootings have slowed in recent months, criminal cases and admissibility hearings involving the extortionists are proceeding at full pace.

Alleged Baweja group members Kawanmeet Singh, Ekamjot Singh and Sukhdeep Singh were all found inadmissible to Canada, because of organized criminality, during separate IRB hearings this summer in Vancouver and Toronto.
A hearing for a fourth alleged Baweja group member — Rohit Nain — is slated for January.

"These four names do appear repeatedly throughout independent police investigations by various agencies. This includes the RCMP, Calgary Police Services, the Surrey Police Service and the CBSA," a lawyer for the Ministry of Public Safety told Ekamjot Singh's hearing.

"They share vehicles, residences, they travel together across the country. They've also been encountered repeatedly during police investigations into various criminal offences that are directly linked to extortion cases."
Extortion threats down but fight isn't over, Surrey police say
'Shady individuals'
Kawanmeet Singh, Ekamjot Singh and Sukhdeep Singh all came to Canada on study permits.
Like the vast majority of alleged Bishnoi gang associates, they are officially referred to by the last name Singh — one of the most common surnames in India — in immigration proceedings.
But for some — like Kawanmeet Singh — Singh turns out to be a middle name.
According to the IRB documents, Kawanmeet Singh's actual surname is Baweja, the name his associates came to identify with his alleged Bishnoi cell.

Police officers escort Lawrence Bishnoi, right, inside a courthouse in New Delhi, India, on April 18, 2023. The Bishnoi gang has taken responsibility for hundreds of extortion attacks across Canada. (Rahul Singh/ANI/Reuters)

The group came under intense scrutiny after the October 2025 college parking lot incident, which police said appeared "to be a planned and retaliatory attack on the Baweja group by members of another gang."
"A van pulled up in front of them and eight or nine people jumped out and charged the victims with weapons," a government lawyer told Kawanmeet Singh's hearing.
"Ekamjot was pepper sprayed and he got into the Mustang and tried to flee, colliding with the attacker's van, a concrete barrier and other parked cars."
According to the IRB documents, police believe the parking lot attack was the work of a rival gang.

The source of the dispute is unclear, but previous IRB records obtained by CBC News have noted other incidents of factional violence — including a shooting in Edmonton — between Bishnoi foot soldiers.

The Canada Border Service Agency's tactical guide to the gang also notes a split between Lawrence Bishnoi and former top lieutenant Goldy Brar — who himself came to Canada on a student visa before vanishing as a wanted man.
Police investigate the scene of a shooting in Surrey in October 2025. A Bishnoi cell known as the Baweja group has been tied to multiple instances of violence in B.C. and Alberta. (Ben Nelms/CBC)
In the hours immediately after the parking lot attack, the Baweja group was allegedly back at work — linked to another extortion-related shooting on the opposite side of Calgary
A car belonging to another group member was caught on CCTV video near a residence, where an assailant pumped nine bullets into a Jeep in the middle of the night.

"When police attend[ed] the home to speak with the owner of the car, there [were] two other individuals in that home that readily advised police that they have been victims of extortion at the behest of the Bishnoi organization," a member of the IRB told Sukhdeep Singh's hearing.

"Further investigation by police reveal[ed] that the owner of the vehicle advised police of his concerns regarding a number of individuals, including yourself ... and you are all referred to as 'shady indviduals.'"
'Call me back'

CCTV footage and ballistic evidence would tie the group and their vehicles to a series of incidents that took place in the Calgary area prior to the parking lot attack, starting with a shooting at a restaurant in September 2025.
The restaurant owner told police he received a WhatsApp call from someone claiming to represent the Bishnoi gang.
"Call me back, otherwise this can happen at your residence next time," the message said. "Call me back when you get up in the morning."
‘We will rule in CANADA’: Bishnoi gang in letter to police
Threats from the same number were linked to shootings at the home and business of the owner of a Calgary tire shop.
"He told police he received multiple calls on his personal and business numbers and the offenders demanded 700,000 dollars and threatened further violence," the IRB documents state.

Forensic evidence showed the same firearm was used at both scenes. Spent casings from the gun were allegedly found alongside a ski mask and Ekamjot Singh's identity documents during a search of the room he shared with Rohit Nain.
According to the IRB documents, the shell casings were also a match for nine other extortion shootings — including one in a series of high-profile attacks at Kap's Cafe in Surrey.
Cross-Canada connections

Owned by Indian celebrity Kapil Sharma, Kap's Cafe has been the frequent target of shootings attributed to Bishnoi through Goldy Dhillon, identified as a kind of North American sub-contractor for the gang.
Shell casings from another shooting at Kap's Cafe also proved instrumental in busting another, separate Bishnoi cell operating out of Edmonton last year.
Multiple members of that group have since been deported from Canada.
Police investigate one of a series of extortion shootings at Surrey's Kap's Cafe. Shell casings from the scene have been tied to guns used by at least two separate Bishnoi cells. (Ethan Cairns/CBC)
The Baweja group's members also appear to have moved frequently between Alberta, B.C and Ontario.
According to the IRB documents, Calgary police arrested Kawanmeet Singh after a brutal assault in a Tim Hortons parking lot on Oct. 13, 2025.

The victim claimed he had been the victim of extortion threats, including messages containing pictures of firearms. He was knocked to the ground and his teeth were kicked in by a group of five or six people who then fled in a variety of vehicles.
Kawanmeet Singh was intercepted behind the wheel of someone else's pickup truck.
"The owner of that vehicle readily admitted that he had lent the car to Mr. [Kawanmeet] and that he had refused to give it back and was now threatening the owner," the documents read.
"And while that car was quite obviously stolen, the owner of that car was very hesitant in reporting that vehicle stolen."

The IRB documents say the Baweja gang has ties to multiple suspects in other extortion cases — including two of the 19 people Calgary police have charged with extortion-related offences — including a planned kidnapping.

"The Baweja sub-group has evidentiary links to multiple extortions and firearm-related offences, not only in Calgary, but in other jurisdictions across Canada," said a police report quoted verbatim at the IRB hearing.
Calgary Sikh community organizes extortion town hall
The report said the Baweja gang members fit a larger profile.

"They are mostly young, East Indian individuals, predominantly arriving on study permits, who often trace their association to friendships formed studying in Canada, or existing friendships they formed in India," the report said.

"The individuals in this sub-group are highly mobile, frequently moving addresses and travelling to Calgary and Surrey, Edmonton and Brampton. The individuals in this group frequently pose with firearms, real and imitation, and openly mock and challenge police."
'They will simply be deported'
The latest IRB documents cite a confidential informant who told police about the gang's inner workings after being "offered money to shoot a video of someone conducting these criminal activities."

"Shooters received their instructions electronically, firearms are left in vehicles for them to use, they are required to provide video proof of the actual attacks or arsons, and payment follows completion of the acts," the informant told authorities.

"Unauthorized use of the Bishnoi name is very uncommon because the organization ... strictly controls the use of their personal brand and there are some very serious consequences if you use it without their permission."

Bullet holes are seen in the glass at Surrey, B.C.'s Radio Swift 1200 AM. The station was the subject of an extortion attack from the leader of Hood 420, another Bishnoi cell identified by CBC News. (Nav Rahi/CBC)
IRB and police documents suggest the existence of multiple cells operating within Canada under the larger umbrella of Lawrence Bishnoi's operation.
CBC News has reported on the existence of Hood 420 — yet another separate cell tied to a shooting at a Surrey radio station.

items: Inside 'Hood 420:' Bishnoi-linked gang tied to threats against B.C. radio station

blocks.text: The confidential witness cited in the IRB documents said the gang recruits through existing street gangs like Surrey's Ruffians and independent sub-groups made of Indian nationals on study permits.
"Only those individuals who are trusted are recruited, and trust is built by the so-called students living together in the same home or apartment," the IRB documents read.

"These individuals are not afraid of Canadian police because the criminal justice system is considered by them to grind slowly and many know that they will simply be deported from Canada without more."
'I want to get back to my parents'
According to the IRB transcripts, Kawanmeet Singh, Ekamjot Singh and Sukhdeep Singh all denied any involvement with the Bishnoi gang.

"Because of my personal circumstances, my financial difficulties, my association with these people in school and the college, I got stuck with these people. I got involved with these people," Ekamjot Singh told his admissibility hearing.
"However, the activities of the Baweja group or anybody else who does that, I take no part in it. I had no interest in it. It was just my circumstances that got me involved with these people."

items: Alleged Bishnoi associate flaunts guns, bullets, cash in video obtained by CBC News
Minister of Public Safety fights to keep accused murderer and alleged Bishnoi gangster in custody

blocks.text: Sukhdeep Singh insisted that he was the victim of a terrible misunderstanding.

"You maintained that this is a case of mistaken identity, that you are not the person of interest, but rather there is another individual who is noted throughout the disclosure who has the same name as you," the IRB tribunal member said.

"Your counsel has argued that this other Sukhdeep Singh is the one who was found in possession of a firearm that may or may not have been used in a number of crimes, and that this is further evidence of a mistake."

items: 'Danger to the public': The story behind the deportation of a 'Ruffian'
Inside an extortion deportation case: The arsons, auto frauds and shootings linking crime across Canada

blocks.text: For his part, accused gang leader Kawanmeet Singh, who has a tattoo of an AK-47 on his neck, insisted that "there is no such group as Baweja group."
"I do not even wish to stay in Canada," he told his IRB hearing, speaking from immigration custody.
"Wherever I am, you know, lodged right now, I am finding it really very, very difficult to stay here. I want to get back to my parents. So that is it. I may please be sent back to my parents."
Bishnoi gang threatened to 'take over Canada' in 2025 letter to police

articles.title: Philippines, UAE go after Filipino visa scammers
articles.summary: The Philippines and UAE are collaborating to pursue visa scammers who duped hundreds of OFWs. The two countries also roll out new digital recruitment systems.

blocks.text: ASSURANCE. Migrant Workers Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac tells Filipino household service workers during a get-together in Dubai on November 7, 2026, that there are legal services and funds available to them.
Jojo Dass/Rappler
The Philippines and UAE are collaborating to pursue visa scammers who duped hundreds of OFWs. The two countries also roll out new digital recruitment systems.

DUBAI, UAE – The Philippines’ Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) is working with the United Arab Emirates’ Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratization (MOHRE) to go after the Filipinos who allegedly victimized fellow Filipinos seeking freelance visas.

“We have coordination with the host government in running after the scammers, protecting victimized visa scams as well as cooperation with respect to addressing and finding those who prey upon OFWs,” DMW Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac told overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) in Dubai on November 7.

Cacdac was in Dubai until November 8 for the fourth Serbisyo Caravan of government agencies to provide one-stop services for OFWs, and for the Salamat Kabayan early Christmas celebration for household service workers.

Rappler earlier reported that two Filipinos — Junie Sorsano, a prominent Dubai-based content creator for over a decade, and Ryan Ronel Baco — allegedly duped some 400 overseas Filipino workers of AED 3.6 million (around P62 million) in visa facilitation.
The victims were mostly domestic helpers, caregivers, and retail sales staff, who sought freelance visas to legally pursue independent, self-sponsored employment.

blocks.caption: Dubai visa scam leaves hundreds of OFWs in financial, legal woes

blocks.text: Cacdac said he had raised the issue during a meeting with MOHRE head Dr. Abdulrahman Abdulmannan Al Awar.
“We have stronger cooperation now,” Cacdac said, noting this was his fourth meeting with Al Awar this year.

“If the alleged visa scammers have already fled UAE and are hiding in the Philippines, we will also talk to the DOJ, to Secretary [Fredderick] Vida about this matter and determine what charges can be filed against them,” he added.
He highlighted that victims can access MWO’s legal services and action fund.
“Rest assured, we have the legal services of our legal retainer that will help victims and in coordination with MOHRE on this issue. We may also tap the action fund on this,” the DMW secretary said.
He urged OFWs to consult the MWO to avoid scams.

Cacdac also signed an agreement with DataFlow Group to pilot the Digital Recruitment and Employer Accreditation Management (DREAM) System, an online platform allowing UAE employers, principals, and recruitment agencies to submit documents and pay fees digitally.
Designed to cut processing time and costs, the system complements MWO Dubai’s Online Employment Contract Verification System (OECVS), which has verified over 100,000 contracts since July 2025.

“Our 20 to 30 people at MWO will not anymore be sitting behind desks doing clerical or documentation work because these can now be done through the digitalized system, which means more of our people will be out there talking to the Filipino community, going to places where the Filipinos usually congregate visit hospitals, visit prisons to deploy legal services,” Cacdac explained.
Cacdac also discussed the upcoming Manila meeting of the Abu Dhabi Dialogue (ADD), which the Philippines will chair in 2027.

Established in 2008 as a voluntary consultative forum and currently chaired by Oman, ADD member states include the UAE, Philippines, Afghanistan, Bahrain, Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Kuwait, Malaysia, Nepal, Pakistan, and Qatar.
The 9th edition (2026–2027) will focus on Artificial Intelligence and digitalization.

Cacdac also visited Pinas Cargo, a logistics firm shipping care boxes to the Philippines, meeting with founder and CEO Marlyn Castro. (READ: Dubai OFWs pay it forward with scholarships for Filipinos back home) – Rappler.com

articles.title: Former NSW Liberal MP Rory Amon found guilty of raping 13-year-old boy
articles.summary:
The 37-year-old was convicted in the state’s supreme court months after a different jury failed to reach a verdict on the same charges

  • Get our

blocks.text: A former NSW Liberal politician is facing the possibility of a significant jail term after a jury found him guilty of raping a 13-year-old boy.

The former MP Rory Amon was found guilty by a jury, after about four hours of deliberation on Friday, of one count of sexual intercourse with a person aged between 10 and 14 and indecently assaulting a child.

The 37-year-old was facing his second NSW supreme court trial after a different jury acquitted him in March on eight separate charges of child sexual offending, but could not reach a verdict on the two counts decided on Friday.
The charges related to Amon’s interactions with a 13-year-old boy who the former MP met on an adults-only website, the court heard.
Amon always maintained his innocence, saying he held an honest and reasonable belief that the boy was over the age of 16.
The original trial was told the boy inflated his age when signing up to the gay hook-up app, and again while talking with Amon.
Amon and the boy exchanged explicit images before a 2017 meeting in the carpark of the boy’s apartment block, the court heard.

At the time he first contacted the youth, Amon was working full-time for the federal MP for Mackellar, Jason Falinski. Amon went on to serve two terms on Northern Beaches council before being elected as the Liberal MP for the state seat of Pittwater in 2023.
The charges scuppered Amon’s fledgling career in state politics, forcing his expulsion from the Liberal party and his resignation after his election in March 2023.
His exit had implications for the state Liberals, which lost the formerly safe seat to a teal independent at the subsequent byelection.
Amon remains on bail and will return to court for a sentencing hearing on 27 November.
after newsletter promotion

He is the third former NSW MP convicted of sexual offences in recent years. The former Kiama MP and Coalition minister Gareth Ward was jailed in 2025 for the sexual abuse of two young men, including a political staffer who was intoxicated after an event at NSW Parliament House. His three-year-nine-month minimum term expires in April 2029.

The former NSW minister Milton Orkopoulos was found guilty in 2023 of sexually abusing teenage boys while he was a state Labor MP. A jury found the 65-year-old guilty of 26 charges of sexual offending against four underage boys and supplying them with drugs over a decade, ending in 2003.
He had already served more than a decade in prison for sexual assault of a minor, indecent assault, supplying heroin and cannabis and other offences.

articles.title: Palace: Apollo Quiboloy extradition 'long overdue'
articles.summary: The issuance of an extradition arrest warrant for Kingdom of Jesus Christ (KOJC) founder Apollo Quiboloy to face criminal charges in the United States is already "long overdue," Malacañang said…

blocks.text: Published November 13, 2026 6:43pm

The issuance of an extradition arrest warrant for Kingdom of Jesus Christ (KOJC) founder Apollo Quiboloy to face criminal charges in the United States is already "long overdue," Malacañang said Friday.

Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said the extradition warrant of arrest and hold departure orders are part of legal procedure, following Manila's receipt of the US government's request to extradite Quiboloy.
She added that the court's issuance merely coincided with the arrival of US President Donald Trump to the Philippines for the 46th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit next week.
"Hindi. Nagkataon lang siguro dahil alam na natin noon pa itong pag-request at voluminous ang documents," Castro said.
(No. It's just a coincidence because we already knew about this request and the documents were voluminous.)
"Kaya medyo natagalan din ang pag-aaral. So long overdue na ito. Maraming nang binasa para makagawa ng petition," she added.
(That's why it took a while to study, so this is long overdue. A lot of documents read to come up with a petition.)
The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) announced last August that it has received the extradition request from the US.
The Makati Regional Trial Court issued an extradition arrest warrant and hold-departure order for Quiboloy and two of his co-accused, the Department of Justice (DOJ) said Friday.

"The court issued an Extradition Warrant of Arrest against the foregoing individuals, after finding probable cause that: (a) each extraditee is the person named in the corresponding foreign arrest warrant and indictment, (b) that the offenses charged are extraditable offenses, and (c) that each extraditee committed the offense or offenses charged," it said in a statement.
"At the same time, said court likewise issued a Hold Departure Order against each extraditee, to prevent any attempt by each of them to depart from the Philippines," it added.
Castro also said President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. is letting the DOJ handle Quiboloy's case.
"Even before, sinabi naman ito ay ipinauubaya niya sa DOJ. So, alam naman niya ang nagiging proseso," Castro said.
(Even before, Marcos said he would leave it to the DOJ. So, he knows the process.)
Also on Friday, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) said it is ready to assist in the extradition of Quiboloy, in coordination with the DOJ and other law enforcement agencies.

The NBI explained that the law enforcement agency holding custody of Quiboloy will be responsible for presenting him in court, noting that the extradition will undergo a process and require a hearing. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Quiboloy unfazed by extradition, prepared for legal battle --lawyer
articles.summary: Kingdom of Jesus Christ founder Apollo Quiboloy was not surprised by the extradition petition filed against him and is prepared to face the proceedings in court, his legal counsel, Atty. Israelito…

blocks.text: Published November 13, 2026 6:15pm

Kingdom of Jesus Christ founder Apollo Quiboloy was not surprised by the extradition petition filed against him and is prepared to face the proceedings in court, his legal counsel, Atty. Israelito Torreon said Friday.

Torreon clarified that he does not represent Quiboloy in the extradition proceedings, noting that his duties are limited to the religious leader's pending criminal cases before the Pasig and Quezon City courts.
He confirmed that Quiboloy has already been notified of the extradition petition, which the Department of Justice (DOJ) filed on Monday on behalf of the United States government.

“Please be informed that Pastor Apollo C. Quiboloy has been informed of the extradition proceedings filed against him. They do not come as a surprise to him. He has expected them, and he is ready to face them in court, through the proper legal process and before the proper forum,” Torreon said in a statement posted on Facebook.
He emphasized that they will answer the allegations against Quiboloy in court, where the matter belongs, rather than in the court of public opinion.
Torreon advised that all inquiries regarding the extradition proceedings be directed to the separate legal team handling that case.

Earlier on Monday, the DOJ confirmed that the Makati Regional Trial Court had issued an extradition arrest warrant and a hold departure order against Quiboloy, who is currently detained at the Pasig City Jail.

Regarding the pending criminal cases against the Davao-based religious leader, Torreon said his client will continue to face the charges and urged the public not to make any assumptions about the issue yet.

“In the criminal cases, we will continue to defend Pastor Quiboloy fully and vigorously. We ask the public and the media to respect the presumption of innocence that the Constitution guarantees to every accused,” Torreon said.

DOJ spokesperson Atty. Raphael “Polo” Martinez said prosecution has finished presenting its evidence in Quiboloy’s qualified trafficking case before the Pasig Regional Trial Court (RTC) and will now formally submit its evidence to the court.

On Monday, DOJ spokesperson Atty. Raphael “Polo” Martinez said the prosecution has finished presenting its evidence in Quiboloy’s qualified trafficking case before the Pasig Regional Trial Court (RTC) and will now formally submit its evidence to the court.
Meanwhile, he said the prosecution is still presenting its evidence in Quiboloy’s pending cases before the Quezon City RTC.
“For the child abuse case under RA 7610 pending before RTC QC, the prosecution is still in the process of presenting its evidence,” Martinez told reporters Friday.
The National Bureau of Investigation has expressed its readiness to coordinate with the DOJ and other law enforcement agencies in Quiboloy’s extradition process. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: What we know about the global Microsoft outage
articles.summary: Microsoft has said the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident, but efforts to fix the issues have so far been largely unsuccessful.
articles.byline: Helen Davidson, Jessica Lamb, Helen Sullivan

blocks.text: Watch: What we know about the Microsoft global outage overnight
ByHelen DavidsonJessica Lamb and Helen Sullivan
A major global Microsoft outage has caused problems, or in some cases disabled entire services, including emails and artificial intelligence products.
Microsoft has said the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident, but efforts to fix the issues have so far been largely unsuccessful.
Here's what we know about the services affected and what went wrong.
What happened?
Microsoft 365 Services, including Teams, Outlook and Microsoft's artificial intelligence software Copilot, have been affected by "connectivity problems".
Customers are reporting varying levels of access - many have not been able to send or receive emails, view certain files or details on their calendar apps.
Some users have been able to use Teams and are using messaging and online meeting functions without issues.
How many people have been affected?
More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps according to Microsoft's website.
The full scale of the outage has not been confirmed, but monitoring website Downdetector had 140,000 people from 74 countries report issues with Outlook on Thursday evening.
The real figure affected is likely much higher because Downdetector relies primarily on users self-reporting.
Microsoft 365 is also used by companies worldwide and is expected to have a knock-on effect to other services.
Tech giants OpenAI and Anthropic have both reported problems as a result of the outage.
ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it was investigating an issue affecting its connections to Microsoft's services, which has caused some tools to not work as expected.
Government agencies and services, including the Singaporean government and Australia's spy agency, have also said they have been affected.
Across the UK, GP surgeries, pharmacies, police and schools have been affected by the outage.

Some GP surgeries have urged patients not to submit messages via their website while the problem remains, while several large police forces are urging members of the public to call if they want to make a report.
What has Microsoft said?
Microsoft has ruled out a cyber-attack and attributed the ongoing outage to "elevated load" on its infrastructure.
The term refers to when servers are handling a much higher volume of stress than they usually do.
In the case of the Microsoft outage, a large number of servers became "unexpectedly unavailable", the company said, which sent added traffic to remaining servers, straining these.
On Friday morning, Microsoft said it was seeing "early signs of stabilisation", but service capacity has "not yet returned to normal levels".
In an earlier statement, the tech giant had said that its attempted fixes were "not taking as expected".
What have experts said?
Australian cyber-security expert Troy Hunt told the BBC the outage could have far-reaching consequences.
"Microsoft is a massive part of the internet backbone and reminds us how critical email still is.

"Not only does this outage affect many people's ability to work but also things like the ability to communicate about appointments, purchase things that need verification, create or access accounts and services," he said.
Paul Spain from New Zealand-based advisory firm Gorilla Technology said that with e-mails and services offline, companies have practically "lost a business day", which is "frustrating" users".

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Old Remulla video misused to falsely claim Dela Rosa has no ICC warrant
articles.summary: A January 2026 interview clip released months before the ICC unsealed the warrant recirculated on social media and was falsely presented as a current update on Dela Rosa’s arrest

blocks.text: Claim: Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Jonvic Remulla said there is no arrest warrant against Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa.
Why we fact-checked this: A reel posted on November 6 by the Facebook page “Pobre Nga Uyamot” shows an interview clip of Remulla with the overlaid text, “Klaro walang warrant (Clearly no warrant).”
Additional overlaid text read: “Walang kaso si Bato sa Pinas! Pag lumaban, mamatay pulis order sa taas ma-blame! High risk! Law of the land pa rin.”
(Bato has no case in the Philippines! If he fights back, police will die and whoever gave the order will be blamed! High risk! The law of the land still applies.)

In the clip, Remulla says: “Si Bato, ano hahanapin namin? ‘Di ba, alam naming nasa Davao siya. Pero wala naman kaming warrant of arrest. Wala. So bakit namin hahanapin? Ba’t namin aarestuhin? Kung gusto niya, siya [ang] mag-citizen’s arrest.”

(Why will we search for Bato? We know he’s in Davao, but we don’t have an arrest warrant. None. So why would we search for him? Why would we arrest him? If he wants to, let him make a citizen’s arrest.)
As of writing, the video has 2.5 million views, 15,000 reactions, 2,300 comments, and 3,400 shares.
The facts: The clip is old and was misleadingly presented as a current update on Dela Rosa’s status as a subject of an International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrant.

The clip was from Remulla’s January 27, 2026 interview on ANC, during which he addressed former senator Antonio Trillanes IV’s suggestion to search for Dela Rosa, who at the time had not been attending Senate sessions amid rumors of an ICC warrant against him.

Remulla then made the remark shown in the Facebook reel, adding that he would personally go to Davao to fetch Dela Rosa. He also suggested that Trillanes could carry out a citizen’s arrest if such a warrant existed.

At the time Remulla said this, the ICC warrant had not been made public. The ICC’s records show it was issued as secret on November 6, 2025, and unsealed only on May 11, 2026, several months after the interview from which the clip was taken.
Dela Rosa is accused of murder for crimes against humanity involving at least 32 killings between July 2016 and April 2018 under the bloody drug war of former president Rodrigo Duterte.

What happened after January: In May, the Supreme Court denied Dela Rosa’s request for a temporary restraining order seeking to block the ICC warrant. Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida then said a valid ICC arrest warrant exists and is now enforceable, allowing the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) and the Philippine National Police (PNP) to effect the senator’s arrest.
Dela Rosa went into hiding shortly after the warrant was issued and is now the subject of a P50-million bounty. (READ: Bato dela Rosa’s escape: Timeline, analyses, opinions from experts)
Manhunt for Dela Rosa: On October 23, Remulla described Dela Rosa as “armed and dangerous.” He also warned that an attempt to arrest the senator by force could result in a “bloodbath.”

Dela Rosa’s camp continues to dispute how the warrant can be enforced. His lawyers argue that no local court has issued an arrest warrant and that the bounty cannot replace domestic judicial procedures that they said were necessary before the senator could be arrested.

Authorities have received at least 500 tips about Dela Rosa’s whereabouts, PNP chief General Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. said on November 9. The NBI has said it hopes to arrest the senator before the year ends. – Cyril Bocar/Rappler.com

Efren Cyril Bocar is a journalist from Llorente, Eastern Samar who graduated with a degree in English Language Studies at the Visayas State University. Cyril is also a graduate of the Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: Philippine Navy to deploy vessels to secure 2026 ASEAN Summit
articles.summary: The Philippine Navy will deploy majority of its vessels under the Naval Defense Command (NDC) to ensure maritime security during the upcoming ASEAN Summit, its spokesperson said Friday.

blocks.text: Published November 13, 2026 5:40pm
The Philippine Navy will deploy majority of its vessels under the Naval Defense Command (NDC) to ensure maritime security during the upcoming ASEAN Summit, its spokesperson said Friday.
Navy spokesperson Captain Marrisa Martinez said the deployment would cover Manila Bay, its maritime approaches, and other strategically significant maritime areas.
"Almost all the ships of the Philippine Navy will be employed for this initiative or for this purpose, which is the ASEAN," Martinez told reporters in an ambush interview.
Among the naval assets to be deployed are the newly acquired offshore patrol vessels BRP Raja Sulaiman and BRP Raja Lakandula.
Martinez said priority patrol areas would include the sea approaches to Manila Bay.
The Navy will also deploy personnel from the Philippine Marine Corps, Naval Special Operations Command, Naval Special Warfare Force, as well as air capabilities.
Martinez assured the public that the ASEAN-related deployment would not affect the Navy's regular operations across the country.
She said vessels operating in the West Philippine Sea would continue their patrols and maritime domain awareness activities, particularly given the security situation in the area.

The Navy's security operations will also continue even after the summit concludes, potentially extending for a week or longer to ensure the safety of delegates who remain in the country, Martinez said. — RSJ, GMA News
